final_task_tree.description:

Three things only:
1. Whether to hire a trainer or do it myself.
2. If hiring — two or three local options with real prices.
3. A week-by-week plan for the first four weeks.

Don't research anything beyond those three.

report.markdown:
## Training Plan: 14-month rescue border collie mix — leash pulling + dog-directed barking

### 1. Hire a trainer, or DIY?
**Recommendation: hire a trainer for a short evaluation + foundations block, then run daily repetitions yourself.**

Loose-leash walking is very DIY-friendly. Dog-directed barking/reactivity is not — it's an emotional/arousal problem, and getting the counter-conditioning and threshold management wrong can make it worse. A high-drive breed like a border collie mix, combined with unknown rescue history, is exactly the profile where a few professional sessions (to set the right protocol and correct your handling) pay for themselves. After that, evenings/weekends are enough to run the plan below yourself.

### 2. Local South Bay options with pricing

| Trainer | Area | Specialty | Price | Contact |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **In Tune Dog Training (Nancy Le)** | San Jose & South Bay | Certified (Academy for Dog Trainers grad); reactivity, fear, aggression, positive reinforcement | Not published — request quote. Market rate for this tier is $150–$300/hr | intunedogtraining.com |
| **D For Dogz (Kaajal)** | San Jose, Santa Clara, Sunnyvale, Mountain View, Los Gatos, etc. | Dedicated **Leash Reactive Dog Foundations Program**, then a follow-on "Reactive to Distinguished Dogs" program | Not published — call for quote | 650-538-3011 |
| **Off Leash K9 Training of San Jose** | San Jose | Structured packages; separate program for dog-aggression/reactivity | Basic Obedience 4-week package = **$800 for 4 private lessons** (covers come/sit/down/place/loose-leash heel); reactivity-specific program priced separately | dogtrainerssanjose.com/prices |

<cite index="14-1">Basic Obedience Training is a 4 Week Program at $800 for 4 Private Lessons covering "Come," "Sit," and "Extended Sit," "Down" and "Extended Down," Place and "Extended Place," and Loose Leash Heel.</cite> <cite index="14-12">Off Leash K9 also has a program specially designed for dogs with aggression or reactivity issues around other dogs.</cite>

<cite index="4-1,4-2">D For Dogz offers a Leash Reactive Dog Foundations Program to build calmer neighborhood walks, followed by a Reactive to Distinguished Dogs program for advanced real-world skills.</cite>

<cite index="2-1,2-2">Nancy Le of In Tune Dog Training is a certified professional dog trainer providing positive reinforcement dog training in San Jose and nearby South Bay communities, helping dogs with fear, reactivity, aggression, and separation anxiety.</cite>

For general budgeting: <cite index="12-9">in Southern California, experienced private trainers charge $150–$300 per hour, while less experienced trainers may charge $80–$125.</cite> Board-and-train (not recommended here — you want to build the skills yourself) <cite index="12-4">ranges from $500 to $1,500 per week.</cite>

**Next step (yours):** call D For Dogz (650-538-3011) and email In Tune Dog Training for quotes and evening/weekend availability; get Off Leash K9's reactivity-program price as a third comparison point.

### 3. Four-week plan

**Week 1 — Foundations & management (no other dogs yet)**
- Switch to a front-clip harness (e.g. Freedom or Easy Walk) or head halter; stop walking on a flat collar/retractable leash.
- Teach "look at me" / name-recognition indoors and in the yard with high-value treats.
- Practice loose-leash walking in the house and driveway — reward every step of slack leash, stop moving the instant the leash tightens ("be a tree").
- Identify your dog's reactivity threshold distance (how far from another dog it can be before reacting) by observing from parked-car distance in a park.
- Book the trainer evaluation session this week if possible.

**Week 2 — Distance work + trainer session**
- Have the professional session (in-person if scheduled) to confirm/correct technique and get a customized counter-conditioning protocol.
- On walks, proactively cross the street or create distance the moment you spot another dog, before your dog reacts — mark and reward calm behavior at that distance ("look, that's a dog — yes! treat").
- Continue loose-leash reps on quiet streets, aiming for 2 short walks/day.

**Week 3 — Shrinking the threshold**
- Gradually decrease the distance at which you can keep your dog calm around other dogs, always rewarding non-reaction rather than waiting for a bark to correct.
- Add duration to loose-leash walking — full block without a pull.
- If using a trainer, second session to review progress and adjust distances/rewards.

**Week 4 — Consolidation**
- Test loose-leash walking in a moderately busy area (still avoiding close passes with reactive triggers).
- Practice a few controlled "parallel walking" exposures at a comfortable distance with a calm dog (arranged in advance, e.g. with a friend's dog or via the trainer) to build positive associations.
- Review with trainer: assess whether you need a follow-on program (D For Dogz's "Reactive to Distinguished Dogs" or equivalent) or can continue independently.

**Ongoing after week 4:** keep sessions short and frequent, keep rewarding calm behavior around triggers indefinitely (this doesn't "graduate" the way obedience does), and increase difficulty (closer distances, busier locations) only as gradually as your dog can handle without reacting.

subtasks.title: Decide DIY vs hiring a trainer
subtasks.description: Recommendation: Hire a trainer, at least for a short evaluation/foundations package, rather than going fully DIY. Reasoning: (1) dog-directed barking/reactivity on leash is a behavior-modification problem, not just an obedience one — technique and timing matter a lot and mistakes (e.g., poor counter-conditioning, flooding) can make reactivity worse; (2) border collies are high-drive, easily over-aroused dogs, and a 14-month rescue may have an unknown history contributing to the reactivity; (3) a few private sessions to get a correct protocol (BAT/counter-conditioning, threshold management, equipment like a front-clip harness) pays off fast, and you can then run the day-to-day repetitions yourself evenings/weekends. Pure DIY is reasonable only for the loose-leash-walking piece; the dog-reactive barking is worth a professional eval given the risk of reinforcing the wrong response.

subtasks.title: Find 2-3 South Bay CA trainers with real prices
subtasks.description:
Three South Bay CA options that explicitly handle leash reactivity, with pricing:

1. **In Tune Dog Training (Nancy Le)** — San Jose & South Bay. Certified professional trainer (Academy for Dog Trainers grad), positive reinforcement, specializes in reactivity/fear/aggression. No published price found on site; request a quote — private in-home sessions in this market typically run $150-$300/hr per market data below. Site: intunedogtraining.com

2. **D For Dogz (Kaajal)** — Serves San Jose, Santa Clara, Sunnyvale, Mountain View, Los Gatos, etc. Runs a dedicated "Leash Reactive Dog Foundations Program" followed by a "Reactive to Distinguished Dogs" program, positive-reinforcement based. Call 650-538-3011 for current pricing (not published online — needs a phone call).

3. **Off Leash K9 Training of San Jose** — Published package pricing: Basic Obedience 4-Week Program = $800 for 4 private lessons (covers come/sit/down/place/loose-leash heel); they also have a separate program specifically for dog-aggression/reactivity issues (price on request). Site: dogtrainerssanjose.com/prices

General market rates for context: private lessons in this region run roughly $150-$300/hr for experienced trainers ($80-$125/hr for less experienced); group classes $30-$80/session; board-and-train $500-$1,500/week. Care.com reports average San Jose trainer rate near $24-25/hr but that figure looks skewed toward dog-walking/daycare gigs, not specialized behaviorist work — treat the $150-300/hr private-lesson figure as the more realistic comp for reactivity work.

Next step (human): call/email In Tune Dog Training and D For Dogz for a quote and to check evening/weekend availability, since exact prices for reactivity-specific work weren't published.
